newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- US DEBT VOLATILITIES FIRM AS BONDS PLUNGE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- US DEBT VOLATILITIES FIRM AS BONDS PLUNGE.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were generally firmer as underlying asset prices plunged, although they were capped by liquidation of old option positions and the weekend time decay, dealers said.

"I think it (slide in underlying markets) took people by surprise," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). But he added that volatilities were relatively calm, considering the market's steep tailspin.
"I think we had some liquidation of long put positions," he said. "We've kind of moved back to the old strikes."
"People who had these puts had been long puts for a long time, so I think they're taking advantage of this opportunity to get out," he added.
Implied volatility for CME December Eurodollar futures options was up about one tenth from Thursday at around 8.8 percent in mid-afternoon, while March volatility rose half a point to 11.2 percent.
December Eurodollar futures fell to a low of 93.950, down from Thursday's 94.070 settlement, before clawing back up a little.

"There's no urgency to buy anthing," the trader noted. "I think that comes from people's experience in the past, being long out-of-the-money volatility and not making any money even when the market goes lower."

Traders said short-August 93.75 puts, a lot of which had been bought in the last few days, were sold off aggessively. Short-August contracts are so-called mid-curve options, which are priced off of 1998 futures but expire in near months.
A T-bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said there was similar liquidation pressure on bond option volatilities as well.
"I think a lot of people had to get out of a lot of stuff on the way down (in bond prices)," he said.
Implied volatility for September T-bond futures options rose nearly a full point on the day to about 8.7 percent. December, which has less gamma, was up 0.3 at 8.6 percent.

Shorter-dated options are richer in gamma, which provides quicker premium accleration and bigger delta changes against movement in bond prices. September options expire in about two-weeks on August 22.
September T-bond futures plunged by two full points to a low of 112-7/32 in the afternoon.
The CBOT trader said there was sporadic but sizeable interest in calls from bottom-pickers as bonds' slide paused.

Traders cited a downturn in the dollar, a pickup in commodity prices as well as distribution problems in the Treasury's newly auctioned notes and bonds as the reason for the market's decline, but said that the environment had not deteriorated that much overall.

"I don't think a lot of people here are selling (futures) to get short," the CME trader said. "They may view the market as having more downside, but I don't think anybody is jumping to conclusions about a near-term Fed tightening or anything."
